subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What are different types of RNA found in the cell?

verification.note: Unit 13 (Biomolecules) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 10 "BIOMOLECULES", book pp.99-104; the book prints this question on book p.100 as VSAQ 17. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The printed answer gives the three names only, with no function. The one-line functions are added here because a question worth two marks is unlikely to be paid in full for three names.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three types
lines: Three types of RNA are found in the cell:
steps.why: All three are single stranded polymers of ribonucleotides; they differ in the job they do in making a protein. Writing both the full name and the short form is worth doing, because the short forms are what the rest of the chapter uses.
common_mistakes: Listing DNA as a type of RNA. DNA is the other nucleic acid, not a kind of RNA.
Giving only the abbreviations. Write the full names as well, since the abbreviations are easy to mix up.
steps.memory_tip: Message, ribosome, transfer: m, r and t.
steps.margin_note: Three names, numbered. That is the first mark on its own.

steps.label: What each one does

lines.text: mRNA carries the code copied from DNA

lines: mRNA carries the code from the DNA in the
rRNA forms part of the ribosome itself,
tRNA brings each amino acid to the ribosome
in the order the code calls for.
steps.why: The three names are far easier to keep apart once each is tied to its job, and the jobs run in a clear order: the message is copied, the ribosome is assembled, the amino acids are delivered. This also answers the follow-up question about how a protein is made.
common_mistakes: Swapping mRNA and tRNA. mRNA carries the code; tRNA carries the amino acid.
Writing that rRNA carries amino acids. rRNA is part of the structure of the ribosome.
steps.memory_tip: m brings the message, t brings the amino acid, r is part of the ribosome.
steps.margin_note: One short line per type. The names alone are usually only half the question.

insider_note: Three names are the first mark; one line each on what they do is the second. Do not stop after the list.
